svg.title: Fig. 86(a) — The graph of y = (1 + 1/x)^x
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 86(a), page 93. Section: exponential.

g.data-text: The axes, the horizontal asymptote y = e (the limit as x → ±∞) and the vertical asymptote x = −1.
For x > 0 the curve rises from the open point (0, 1) towards the asymptote y = e; for x < −1 it comes down from +∞ at the line x = −1 to the same asymptote.
Between x = −1 and x = 0 the base is negative. The points that exist (x a rational with odd denominator) lie on the dotted curves y = ±|1 + 1/x|^x, which both end at the open point as x → 0.
